title: Embedding and Reranker Continuity — Delta Detector + Canary Rollback Playbook
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Problem: Model or configuration changes (new embedding model, quantization profile, ANN index changes, or reranker tuning) can introduce subtle regressions in recall/precision that only surface in production traffic. Current alerts catch gross drift but lack a continuity-first automated canary that ties distributional deltas to offline metric regressions and provides an actionable rollback path.
technical_design:
Summary: Build a Delta Detector service + Canary Runner that runs whenever model/config changes are proposed. Components:

1) Delta Detector (service): computes lightweight distributional deltas between baseline and candidate artifacts using: population stability index (PSI) on embedding norms, pairwise cosine delta histograms, KS-test on score distributions, and a JS divergence sketch for approximate embedding distributions. Delta Detector emits a scored delta vector and a human-readable summary.

2) Canary Runner (pipeline): given a candidate change, runs an offline evaluation suite over pinned holdout prompt sets and production-sampled user queries (privacy-safe) to compute recall@k, precision@k, NDCG, and reranker AUC. The runner compares metrics to baseline, computes effect sizes and statistical significance, and attaches artifacts: per-prompt diffs, top-k failure cases, and ANN index recall traces.

3) Risk Scorer and Policy Engine: maps delta vectors + offline eval outcomes to a risk score. Policies (configurable) dictate automatic canary approval, flag for manual review, or block deployment. Policy examples: block if recall@20 drops >1.5% and PSI > 0.05; escalate if reranker AUC delta p-value < 0.01 and effect size > 0.02.

4) Canary Rollback Playbook: automated rollback orchestration that can revert model/config in the control plane, notify stakeholders with precomputed rollback artifacts, and open an incident if rollout had customer impact.

Implementation notes: Delta Detector is implemented as a serverless microservice backed by Presto queries for aggregate histograms and an ANN diff job that samples 100k probe queries. Canary Runner uses existing offline eval harness (job: eval/emb-rerank-canary) extended to collect per-config artifacts. Persistent artifacts stored in s3://redwood-evals/canary/{run_id}.
acceptance_criteria: Delta Detector service returns a numeric delta vector + human summary for any pair of (baseline, candidate) artifacts within 3 minutes
Canary Runner completes the offline eval on standard holdout (10k queries) within 90 minutes and uploads artifacts to the canonical bucket
Policy engine evaluates risk and produces one of three actions: approve, require-review, block — based on configurable thresholds
Automated rollback action integrates with control plane and successfully reverts a canary deployment in staging during end-to-end test
Dashboard in Grafana shows per-run delta metrics, top failure queries, and trend lines for recall@k over time
rollout_plan: 1) MVP in staging: run Delta Detector + Canary Runner as part of model PR job for embeddings and rerankers. 2) Pilot with internal product teams for two weeks; collect feedback on thresholds and attention signals. 3) Tune policy thresholds using historical experiments (backfill via archived artifacts). 4) Gradual enablement: allow automatic 'require-review' for non-critical tenants, block for reserved capacity customers after approval. 5) Full prod rollout with alerting, runbooks, and 24/7 on-call coverage for the first week.
tests: Unit tests for PSI, KS, JS divergence modules and approximate sketches
Integration test: simulate candidate embedding model with synthetic shift and verify Delta Detector flags expected deltas
End-to-end canary test: create staging canary, run rollback playbook, and validate control-plane revert completes within SLO
Backfill validation: run Canary Runner on three historical model changes to validate thresholds and false positive rate
